inputs.source: Employee question submitted via SSO-authenticated chat session
HR-maintained published policy documents, read-only to the agent, two-person review required before publish

instructions.note: The rule 'Do not give legal advice' is enforced only through a behavioral instruction, with no structural check backing it. Given the agent's read-only scope over internal-sensitivity, HR-reviewed content and its lack of other capabilities, the consequence of a lapse is limited to misinformation, so severity is low.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: The credential grants read-only access to the policy index only. This cannot be defeated by model behavior; the model cannot use access it does not have.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial, verified by pen test
controls.decay_rationale: Egress is blocked at the network layer and independently pen-tested. A more capable or fully adversarial model cannot open a new egress channel that the network does not permit.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links; reply bound to the requester's own session
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the chat client, not the model. A more capable model cannot make the client fetch or render content it does not already support, and the reply destination is fixed to the same authenticated principal who asked the question.

controls.name: Two-person review required before publishing policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the HR publishing workflow, outside the model. It substantially reduces the likelihood of malicious or erroneous content entering the trusted index, but does not fully prevent insider collusion or a future unreviewed content source, so it narrows rather than severs the path.

controls.name: Model version pinned; change requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: The model cannot be silently upgraded; a change ticket is required. This keeps the model_upgrade trigger from firing without review, though the ticket process itself should be watched.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies entirely on the model choosing to follow the instruction; a more capable or adversarially prompted model could rationalize an exception.

findings.title: Authenticated employee question answered from published internal policy content

attack_path.note: Employee submits a question through the authenticated chat session.
Agent searches the published, internal policy index.
Agent replies with a quoted policy excerpt to the same authenticated session.

evidence.observation: Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session, the same principal who asked the question, so source and recipient are the same trusted party.
The policy index holds only published, internal-sensitivity content; no confidential or restricted data is in scope.

recommendations.action: Log question/answer pairs (without extra PII) for periodic HR review to catch drift or misquoted policy text.

findings.title: Internal policy content, if compromised, is relayed verbatim to employees (internal-source goal manipulation)

attack_path.note: HR-authored content enters the published policy index after two-person review.
Agent retrieves the content in response to an employee question.
Agent quotes/relays the retrieved content, including any embedded instructions or errors, to the employee.

forecast.watch_signal: The policy index begins ingesting content from a source other than the HR content team's two-person-reviewed publish workflow (for example, a vendor feed, an unreviewed draft folder, or an automated import), or the two-person review requirement is weakened or removed.

evidence.observation: Only the HR content team can write to the policy index, and publishing requires two-person review; this is the only preventive control between document authorship and the agent's read access.
The only tool is policy_search.search; the model has no independent way to verify the integrity of returned content beyond trusting the index.
The agent is instructed to quote the retrieved policy directly, so text present in an indexed document is relayed close to verbatim to the employee.

recommendations.action: Require the same two-person review gate for any future content source added to the policy index, and treat any unreviewed or externally sourced content as untrusted until reviewed.
Alert security or compliance whenever a new source or a bulk change is made to the policy index, independent of the publishing review.

rating.rationale: The agent's own function (answer employee questions from published HR policy) is low risk: the requester is authenticated and trusted, replies stay within that same session, the chat client does not render or auto-fetch links, and the agent holds only a read-only, least-privilege credential with no network egress, verified by pen test, and no other tools or memory. The one meaningful path is that policy content, though internally authored, is quoted close to verbatim into replies; today this is credibly narrowed (not severed) by mandatory two-person review before publish, giving a residual of low. The forecast rises to high because the two-person review is the single control standing between an internal-trust source and an egress-classified sink (chat reply carrying internal data outside the model boundary): if the policy index's data scope expands to a source that is not put through the same reviewed publish workflow (a vendor feed, an unreviewed draft folder, an automated import), or if that review requirement is removed or weakened, the effective source trust for the new content drops toward untrusted while the sink classification is unchanged, and the two-person review control provides no coverage for it. That single control, ctl.two_person_review, is the one whose decay moves the forecast the most; the network egress denial and the read-only credential are independent of model capability and do not decay under any of the listed triggers.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, tools.json, and runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior, logs, or an independent penetration test by this assessor.

Controls described as verified (network egress denial) or otherwise asserted by the design team (read-only credential scope, two-person review process) were not independently re-verified in this assessment; confidence for those specific claims should be treated as medium rather than high until independently confirmed.

Explicit step and runtime limits for the agent were not stated in the artifacts. This assessment inferred a bounded, single-turn interaction (one search, one reply per question) from the system prompt and the A3 autonomy designation; confirm explicit runtime and step caps in the deployment configuration.

No MCP configuration, agent card, or peer-agent connections were provided or appear applicable, since the agent has a single first-party tool and no delegation. If tools, MCP servers, or peer agents are added, the protocols[] section must be completed and this assessment rerun under the new_tool, new_mcp_server, and new_peer_agent triggers.
